messages:
Anna: We need to lock down model-family specific quotas and burst behavior before the Dedicated launch. Proposal: enforce per-org and per-key limits, but have separate buckets for small/medium/large model families. Thoughts?
Mike: +1 to families. Question: enforcement where? edge gateway (fast reject) or mixer (centralized accounting)?
Jess: edge for latency-critical rejects, but mixer for consistent accounting and cross-region quotas. We might need both: edge does a cheap check for obvious overuse, mixer does final accounting and chargeback.
Sam: Console UX asks for a way to set family overrides and temporary burst grants. Product wants per-org defaults and per-key overrides (api key scoped). Also need an audit trail for manual grants.
Priya: Telemetry requirement: per-family token consumption, burst credit usage, 95/99th percentile rejection rates, and per-key breakdown for support. Dashboards must show both tokens/sec and requests/sec because embeddings vs completion patterns differ.
Mike: Implementing both checks increases complexity. Could do this: edge keeps a fast in-memory token window for rate; mixer persists burst credits in Redis and reconciles asynchronously. If edge allows and mixer later sees overdraw, it can mark and throttle future requests.
Anna: That sounds reasonable. How to handle model-size differences? Example: gpt-small uses 1x token weight, gpt-medium 2x, gpt-large 4x for quota deduction. Are we comfortable with integer multipliers?
Jess: Multipliers are fine but need clear mapping in config and in billing docs. Also need special-case for streaming where we charge as tokens emitted.
Sam: Console mock: per-org page with family sliders (monthly quota, burst credit pool) and a modal to grant temporary +burst credits with expiry. Also "auto-fallback" toggle to route to compatible smaller family when quota exceeded.
Priya: Fallback routing is scary for quality regressions. Telemetry must label all fallback responses so product can filter. Also add an eval that runs on fallback to detect regressions.
Mike: Pseudocode for enforcement I sketched:```python
# on request at edge
weight = model_family_weights[request.model_family]
if org.burst_credit >= weight * request.tokens:
    allow && decrement_in_memory_credit()
else:
    forward_to_mixer()

# mixer does durable check and final decrement in Redis
```
Anna: Good. How should burst credits refill? Simple daily refill vs token-leaky-bucket? I prefer leaky-bucket to smooth spikes.
Jess: Leaky-bucket with configurable refill rate per family. E.g. large models refill slower. Also keep a hard cap so you can't accumulate indefinitely.
Sam: For UI we need to expose current burst balance and next refill ETA. That means we need an endpoint that returns: {balance, cap, refill_rate, next_tick}. Keep response small for polling.
Priya: Metrics: counter for "quota.enforced", "quota.shadow.rejected", "quota.fallback.count", labels: org_id, key_id, model_family. Shadow mode is critical for 2 weeks before any hard rejects.
Mike: Rollout plan: shadow for 14 days, then 5% of traffic hard-enforced (routing by sampling in gateway), then 25%, 100% over 3 weeks. Keep an automatic rollback trigger on support-ticket spike or SLO errors.
Anna: Who owns the config schema? We need a single source of truth that Console and mixer both read. I propose storing YAML configs in ConfigSvc with strong validation and a read cache.
Jess: Agree. Schema example:```yaml
families:
  small:
    weight: 1
    refill_per_min: 10000
    cap: 50000
  medium:
    weight: 2
    refill_per_min: 5000
    cap: 20000
  large:
    weight: 4
    refill_per_min: 1000
    cap: 5000
policies:
  per_org_default: true
  key_override_allowed: true
```
Sam: Need an admin-only API for emergency grants: POST /orgs/:org_id/grants {family: 'large', amount: 10000, expires_at: '...'} and audit log.
Priya: Also add a compliance view showing which orgs had >50% fallback in a week. Legal asked for that for enterprise customers.
Mike: Edge implementation detail: keep per-key in-memory counters sharded by worker. Use consistent hashing for keys to reduce cross-worker reconciliation. Mixer will reconcile via periodic heartbeat.
Anna: Tests: unit tests for weighting, integration tests for synchronous edge->mixer flow, chaos tests for Redis outage (should fall back to permissive or conservative mode?).
Jess: In Redis outage we should fail closed for premium enterprise orgs? Hmm - probably fail open for free-tier, fail closed for paid-with-SLA orgs? That sounds backwards. Let's explicitly define: default = fail open (don't block), enterprise-SLA = fail to conservative enforcement (allow only if edge has enough local credit). We'll document behavior.
Sam: UX note: show "enforcement mode" (shadow/partial/enforced) and allow ops to toggle sample percent. Must be audit logged.
Priya: Alerts: spike in shadow.rejected -> slack #incidents; spike in enforced rejects -> #support. Also create periodic report for customers hitting >=90% quota to prompt upsell.
Anna: Action items: Mike + Jess implement edge + mixer prototype; Priya to draft telemetry and dashboards; Sam to wire Console mock and admin grant API; I'll own rollout plan and policy docs.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: Deployment started for branch feature/quota-families on cluster prov-3. Build 5042.
Mike: I'll start a spike PR and include the YAML schema and integration tests. Expect draft by EOD tomorrow.
Jess: I'll prototype the Console slider and the grants modal; need API shape from Mike.
Sam: I'll add the mock to Figma and share link.
Anna: OK, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene in 48h with PRs and telemetry sketches. :thumbsup:
